Commentary.Commentary: Time to turn to the main event - That brings the curtain down on the final warm-up match, and it was Australia Women who signed off in style with a comfortable win over West Indies Women. But now, the warm-ups are done, the preparations are complete, and the stage is set for the real thing. The ICC Women's T20 World Cup 2026 gets underway on Friday, 12th June, with hosts England Women taking on Sri Lanka Women at Edgbaston, Birmingham. The action begins at 5.30 pm GMT, and as always, we'll be with you well before the first ball for all the build-up, news, and analysis. Until then, take care, and goodbye!

The victorious skipper of Australia Women - Sophie Molineux says that it was a good game and there are a few places they need to work on, but they are overall pleased with the result. She adds that it's good to see Voll get runs and everyone did well. Sophie reckons that it's a bit tricky to choose 11 players, but they will try to balance their squad, and their preparation has been good. She ends by saying that they need to start strongly against South Africa Women, so for now they will get some rest and give their best.

The captain of West Indies Women - Hayley Matthews says that they are monitoring the situation of Henry and hopefully, she will be fine for the first game. She reckons that Voll was brilliant with the bat, and they failed with the ball. Matthews mentions that they have a lot of positives to take from this game. Says that they have a lot of spinners on their side so it's a good sign. She ends by saying that the opening game is important, and they will need to show up against the New Zealand Women.
Let's hear from the captains now...

Henry's injury overshadows the defeat - West Indies Women needed early wickets but were unable to find one in the Powerplay, despite creating a couple of run-out opportunities that went begging. Their troubles in the field continued with dropped catches and sloppy ground fielding, allowing Australia to stay firmly in control of the chase. Hayley Matthews, Qiana Joseph and Karishma Ramharack picked up a wicket each during a brief middle-overs fightback, but the game had already drifted away by then. More than the defeat, though, West Indies will be concerned about Chinelle Henry, who suffered a nasty shoulder injury and had to be stretchered off the field in a distressing sight.

Windies crumble under pressure - Earlier in the game, West Indies Women were bowled out for a below-par total, with Deandra Dottin waging a lone battle through her 46 off 38 balls. In fact, extras ended as their joint-third-highest scorer, a telling reflection of their struggles with the bat. The innings unraveled during a stunning middle-order collapse, with six wickets falling for just 22 runs as Australia tightened their grip on the contest. The Australians were clinical from start to finish, with Lucy Hamilton and Ashleigh Gardner claiming two wickets each, while every bowler apart from Alana King chipped in. Backed by sharp catching and disciplined fielding, it was a complete performance that left West Indies with a mountain to climb.

Aussies cruise home with plenty to spare - Chasing a modest target, Australia Women's openers were in no rush, taking a few overs to assess the conditions before shifting through the gears. Beth Mooney was the first to break free, finding the gaps with ease and racing to 34 off just 18 balls before retiring out shortly after the Powerplay. Georgia Voll had a quieter start, but once she settled in, she looked in complete control. Even though Ellyse Perry, Ashleigh Gardner and Annabel Sutherland failed to make significant contributions, Voll took charge of the chase, bringing up a fluent half-century and ensuring there were no late hiccups as she stayed till the end on 77* off 48 to guide Australia home with 30 balls to spare.

Australia tick all the boxes - Australia Women have cruised to victory, making it two wins from two warm-up matches and sending an early reminder to the rest of the field that they are serious contenders for the trophy once again. It was another polished display from the most successful team, who looked in control for most of the contest. For West Indies Women, it is a second straight defeat, but the results will matter far less than the lessons learned and the search for their best combination ahead of the tournament.
